description: Fig. 2 is a composite of three panel groups — (a), (b) and (c) — each containing a Vickers-hardness evolution line plot and a matching two-dimensional hardness contour map, for the 15Al, 17Al and 19Al Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density alloys respectively. Every line plot has y-axis "Vickers hardness (HV)" (0-1100) and x-axis "Aging time (h)" (0-11), with six series labelled in the legend "525 °C Aging", "550 °C Aging", "575 °C Aging", "600 °C Aging", "625 °C Aging" and "650 °C Aging". Markers are open symbols (circles in (a), squares in (b), diamonds in (c)) with error bars on intermediate times. All curves converge at about 250 HV at 0 h and harden rapidly within 1-3 h; the 600 °C series reaches the highest plateau (>900 HV), whereas the 525 °C series of (b) and (c) stays lowest (~500-620 HV at 10 h). Each contour map plots "Aging temperature (°C)" (525-650) against "Aging time (h)" (0-10) with a "Vickers hardness (HV)" colour bar from 250 to 1000 in 50 HV steps, contoured 400.0-900.0. The >900 HV red field covers most conditions in (a) and (b), but in (c) it is confined to a small region near 575-600 °C at ~4-9 h, showing the alloy-dependent aging-hardening window.

observations.observation: Each line plot in (a), (b) and (c) has y-axis "Vickers hardness (HV)" spanning 0-1100 and x-axis "Aging time (h)" spanning 0-11.
The legend common to all three line plots lists exactly six aging conditions: "525 °C Aging", "550 °C Aging", "575 °C Aging", "600 °C Aging", "625 °C Aging" and "650 °C Aging".
Marker style differs between panels: open circles in (a), open squares in (b), open diamonds in (c), each series carrying vertical error bars on the 1 h, 3 h and 6 h points.
In all three panels the six curves converge at approximately 250 HV at 0 h aging time (markers overlap near the 250 HV gridline).
In panel (a) the 600 °C series lies above 900 HV from 1 h to 10 h and is the highest curve for most of the aging time.
In panel (b) the 575 °C series peaks highest of all curves, near the 900-1000 HV range at 6 h, then decreases by 10 h; the 525 °C series is the lowest, only slightly above 600 HV at 10 h.
In panel (c) the 600 °C series is highest (~900-920 HV) and the 525 °C series is lowest (about 590-620 HV at 10 h).
The contour maps use y-axis "Aging temperature (°C)" over 525-650, x-axis "Aging time (h)" over 0-10, and a colour bar titled "Vickers hardness (HV)" running from 250 to 1000 in 50 HV bands.
Contour isolines labelled 500.0, 600.0, 700.0, 800.0 and 900.0 are printed on the maps; in (c) an additional 400.0 label appears near the low-temperature corner.
In the (a) contour map a large red field corresponding to the >900 HV colour band occupies most aging times above roughly 3 h across 600-650 °C.
In the (c) contour map the >900 HV red region is much smaller than in (a), forming a compact island near 575-600 °C between about 3 and 9 h.
The caption states that (a), (b) and (c) correspond to the 15Al, 17Al and 19Al alloys, respectively, after different aging treatments.

The caption contains a trailing fragment, "length starting from the indentation corners, as schematically illus trated in Fig. 1", which does not match anything visible in these panels — it appears to be mis-joined text belonging to Fig. 1.

Citing text states that the hardness of the solution-treated alloys increased with rising Al content owing to solid-solution strengthening, and that unusual rapid aging hardening occurred in all three alloys.
Citing text and abstract report the achieved hardness range as 253.4 HV to 965.6 HV (the citing sentence is truncated at "253.4 HV to").

subfigures.description: 15Al alloy. Left: Vickers hardness (HV) vs Aging time (h) plot, six aging-temperature series (525-650 °C) as open circles with error bars; all start near 250 HV, the 600 °C curve is the highest (>900 HV from 3 h on), the 550 °C curve rises most slowly (about 380 HV at 1 h, ~790 HV at 3 h). Right: hardness contour map, Aging temperature 525-650 °C vs Aging time 0-10 h, colour bar 250-1000 HV; contour labels 500.0, 600.0, 700.0, 800.0; a large red >900 HV field occupies most aging times above ~3 h and high temperatures.

17Al alloy. Left: same hardness vs aging time plot with open-square markers; 600 °C is highest at 1 h (~860 HV), 575 °C peaks near 930 HV at 6 h and then falls, while 525 °C remains lowest (about 570-620 HV). Right: corresponding contour map with labels 400.0, 500.0, 700.0, 800.0, 900.0; the >900 HV red region is a broad band roughly between 600 and 650 °C and an isolated island around 575-600 °C at ~5-9 h.

19Al alloy. Left: same plot with open-diamond markers; 600 °C is the highest series (~900-920 HV), 625 °C and 650 °C plateau near 800-860 HV, and 525 °C stays lowest (~590-620 HV). Right: contour map with labels 400.0, 500.0, 600.0, 700.0, 800.0, 900.0; the >900 HV red field is restricted to a compact region near 575-600 °C between about 3 and 9 h, and a 700.0 HV contour bounds the mid-temperature plateau.
